newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas steady in thin trade, some prompt demand.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas steady in thin trade, some prompt demand.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market was little changed from Friday's levels in thin trade on Monday, traders and brokers said, although some dealers said it was interesting that prices did not fall.

"It seems to have a bit of strength," said a trader. He pointed out that there had been system buys on the flexibility mechanism on Friday, Saturday and Monday, reaching a maximum price of 10.29 pence a therm on Saturday.
"It's interesting that it (the system) bought," he said, "it may have added strength."
Both the day ahead and the balance of April were done at 10 pence on the physical market.
The day ahead market had been discussed and traded below 10 pence on Friday, although this relative weakness partly reflects the fact that day ahead demand is generally lower before the weekend.
Day ahead prices went even higher towards the close, with one trader reporting a deal at 10.25 pence a therm.
Further out, there was some trade done in the third, fourth and first quarters at prices which were closely in line with Friday's levels, although there was weakness seen in the first quarter.
But activity was thin, with dealers explaining the slow pace as "a typical Monday in the gas trade," and one saying "there's still a bit of Easter effect going on."

The futures market had earlier been extremely quiet, with no trade at all done in the morning session and only 25 lots traded in four deals in the afternoon. The only months to trade were June and November, with prices little changed.

Transco reports that Tuesday's gas demand is forecast to reach 227 mcm or 53 percent of peak day demand, with the temperature expected to reach 9.1 Celsius, 0.3 Celsius above the seasonal normal level.
